item.title: Laopu Gold and the Return of Chinese Luxury on Chinese Terms
item.description:
In the middle of one of the most difficult years for Western luxury in China, a category of brands barely known outside the country was posting extraordinary growth.

Heritage-gold jewellery — specifically brands like Laopu Gold and Lao Feng Xiang, whose aesthetic vocabulary draws entirely from Chinese craft traditions, Chinese materials, and Chinese cultural logic — became the most dynamic luxury category in the market. With soaring profits and rapidly expanding store networks, these heritage-gold jewellery brands are red-hot in China’s otherwise tepid luxury market.

item.title: Korea Spends More on Luxury Per Capita Than Anyone Else on Earth. Here's Why.
item.description:
The statistic lands differently depending on where you encounter it.

In a Morgan Stanley research note, it is a data point — interesting, filed, moved on from. In a conversation with a Seoul native about their relationship with fashion, it is a revelation of something they have always known but never seen quantified. South Koreans spend more on luxury goods per capita than any other population on Earth.

Total spending on personal luxury goods by South Koreans grew around 24% year-on-year to $16.8 billion, amounting to $325 per capita — the highest in the world.

item.title: Louis Vuitton Is Building Worlds in Asia
item.description:
There is a scene playing out across Asia’s luxury capitals that tells you everything about where the industry is heading. It does not take place in a store.

In Seoul, Louis Vuitton has opened LV The Place — a six-storey complex that combines retail, exhibition space, café culture, and fine dining into a single vertical brand world. In Singapore, the maison operates L’Appartement, a quieter, more intimate environment for top-tier clients. In Tokyo, the experience multiplies again — different city, different register, same coherent universe.
